userStories.name: Preserve Vertex added-object primary keys
userStories.description: When users add OSS objects into a Vertex graph, preserve the selected object's primary key so the selection sidebar can fetch fresh properties, time-series, and activity for newly added nodes instead of degrading to stale or empty local metadata.
bdd_acceptance: Given the Add Objects dialog receives OSS search rows with `__rid`, `__primaryKey`, and a title property, When the user checks rows and clicks Add, Then the `onAdd` payload carries each row's `primaryKey` alongside rid, label, ontology, and object type.

Given a Vertex workspace graph has newly added nodes from the dialog, When the user selects one of those nodes, Then the Properties tab calls `/api/v2/ontologies/{ontology}/objects/{objectType}/{primaryKey}` with the preserved primary key and renders the fresh object value.
Given an OSS row omits `__primaryKey`, When it is added, Then the dialog falls back to the current label/rid behavior without throwing.

userStories.name: Resolve Vertex overlay time-series sparklines
userStories.description: Replace the Vertex node overlay's time-series glyph placeholder with the same mini-sparkline behavior used by the selection sidebar when object metadata is available.
bdd_acceptance: Given a visible Vertex node has a time-series extended label and object metadata, When the overlay renders, Then it requests that property's stream points and draws a deterministic mini-sparkline from numeric values.
Given stream points are missing, non-numeric, or object metadata is unavailable, When the overlay renders, Then it keeps a clear pending marker and does not throw.
Given many graph nodes exist but only a subset is visible, When the overlay virtualizes cards, Then time-series requests are limited to rendered cards.

userStories.name: Surface Vertex scenario run routes in server contract
userStories.description: Audit the existing Vertex scenario-run package against server wiring and OpenAPI so the scenario execution lifecycle is either mounted and documented or explicitly gated by a focused contract test.
bdd_acceptance: Given `pkg/vertex/scenarioruns` exposes start, cancel, and get handlers, When the server contract test walks registered routes, Then the intended public scenario-run routes are covered by either OpenAPI operations or an explicit non-mounted wiring assertion.
Given scenario-run routes are mounted, When the OpenAPI contract is parsed, Then request and response schemas describe run RID, scenario RID, status, attempts, checkpoints, and cancellation behavior.

Given scenario-run dependencies are not yet production-wired, When the contract test runs, Then it fails with a precise actionable message rather than silently leaving the package as unreachable code.
